user.t:
You are a Senior Code Reviewer with expertise in software architecture, design patterns, and best practices. Your job is to review completed work against its plan or requirements and identify issues before they cascade.

## What Was Implemented
PR-A "Windows correctness" for the ruflo-console Claude Code plugin (TypeScript function-hooks mod, plugins/ruflo-console), 8 commits on branch fix/console-windows in the worktree C:\Users\mariu\ruflo-wt-console-win:
A1 test fixture accepts Windows drive paths; A2 one path helper module (hooks/data/paths.ts) used at every "/"-only absolute-path guard (+ case-folded protected autopilot dirs); A3 home folder falls back to USERPROFILE; A4 disk writes on Windows through the host file API (`writeVia`, flavor 'host-fs') incl. clearable autopilot KILL flag; A5 no Linux-only /proc probe off Linux + cleared probe timers; A6 a successful hive start is re-verified once after 1 s before reporting "expected a queen…".

## Requirements / Plan
Plan: C:\Users\mariu\ruflo\docs\superpowers\plans\2026-10-10-ruflo-console-windows-nav-chat.md — read the header, Global Constraints, Review Focus and the PR-A section only (PR-B and PR-C are separate branches, out of scope).
Ledger with every ruling and every deferred minor finding from the per-task reviews: C:\Users\mariu\ruflo-wt-console-win\.superpowers\sdd\2026-10-10-ruflo-console-windows-nav-chat\progress.md — triage the "minor (deferred)" lines and the "Ruling:" lines: say which must be fixed before merge and which can ship as documented follow-ups.

## Git Range to Review
Base: 24774b9087dad6583a9018c535cee81859262bdc  Head: b2ee1c079
The full package (commit list, stat, diff with context, 177 KB) is already written to one file — read it instead of re-deriving: C:\Users\mariu\ruflo-wt-console-win\.superpowers\sdd\2026-10-10-ruflo-console-windows-nav-chat\review-24774b908..b2ee1c079.diff
Review in passes if needed and say so.

## The spec is a vision document
For behaviour the plan is silent on, judge by what a reasonable person using this console on Windows (and, unchanged, on Linux/macOS) would expect; a spec's silence is not permission.

## Declined to judge
Before your verdict, list every behaviour you considered and set aside as outside the plan, one line each, with the reason.

## Read-Only Review
Do not mutate the working tree, index, HEAD or branches. One focused vitest run is allowed to settle a concrete doubt: from C:\Users\mariu\ruflo-wt-console-win\plugins\ruflo-console run `node node_modules/vitest/vitest.mjs run tests/<file>.spec.ts -t "<name>"`. Known environment-only failures on this machine (not regressions): specs that need sibling plugins or v3/docs (sparse checkout), symlink EPERM, Windows file modes, a '>' in a file name, `claude-code/testing` package missing for .test.ts under vitest, 5000 ms kit-runner timeouts.

## You Do Not Dispatch Subagents

## What to Check
Plan alignment (all of A1–A6 present; deviations justified); cross-task consistency (do A2's path helpers, A3's home and A4's writeVia agree with each other — e.g. paths joined with '/' onto a Windows home then handed to writeVia/below/checkNoLinks; any call site that still builds a POSIX argv on Windows; any write path that bypasses writeVia); security (traversal/containment, protected dirs, link refusal, confirm gate before writes, model-callable tools); Linux/macOS byte-identity; error handling; tests; PR readiness (CHANGELOG/version per ADR-478 are NOT yet done — the controller adds them at PR time; do not flag their absence).

## Output Format

### Issues (#### Critical / #### Important / #### Minor — each with file:line, what's wrong, why it matters, how to fix)
### Deferred-minor triage (one line per ledger item: must-fix-before-merge | follow-up, with reason)

### Recommendations

resp.t:
A search I started in the background, looking for Claude Code's type definitions (`claude-code.d.ts`), hit its time limit and was stopped. I won't restart it, because it would not change the review.

That search was meant to confirm how the engine's file functions (`$.fs.write` and `$.fs.stat`) behave on Windows. Without the definitions, I took the code's own stated behaviour as given, and my report already lists that under "Declined to judge". The real check is the hands-on Windows test the plan asks for.

The report has already gone to you, and its verdict stands: **ready to merge with fixes**. The three fixes:

1. **Autopilot duplicate-start guard:** on Windows, two console sessions can both start the same autopilot step.
2. **Autopilot safety checks on Windows paths:** they miss paths written with backslashes. A task can then point at the autopilot's own settings folder, or at a folder outside the approved list.
3. **Saved console state keys:** the same project opened as `C:\Users\...` and as `c:\users\...\` gets two separate saved states, which the plan said must not happen.

Turning the autopilot off on Windows for now would cover the first two.

handback.t:
## PR-A "Windows correctness" final review (24774b908..b2ee1c079)

I read the review package in two passes: production code (diff lines 54–2150), then tests (2150–3147). I also grepped the live worktree for every write path, every `killSeen`/`pathAllowed`/`startedCount` caller and every remaining "/"-only guard. I made one non-mutating `node` check of the autopilot regexes. I did not run vitest.

### Strengths
- **All six tasks are present.**
  - A1: fixture normalisation.
  - A2: `paths.ts`, used at all 11 sites the plan lists plus `cost-ledger`.
  - A3: `homeOf` wired into `host.home`.
  - A4: `host-fs` flavor plus `writeVia`, with every write call site moved onto it.
  - A5: no `/proc` spawn off Linux; `settleWithin` clears its timer.
  - A6: the bounded 1 s re-verify, following the ruling.
- **Linux/macOS write argv is byte-identical**, and this is pinned well. `write-flavor.spec.ts` has GNU literals and whole-set sha256 digests for GNU and BSD. A test also proves `writeVia('gnu'|'posix')` makes exactly the old `host.run(argv, timeout, stdin)` call. I checked each call-site mapping by hand (`ensureIgnored`, `rotate`, `replaceFile`, `writeNew`, the `statusSpec` replace, the journal append/touch, the archive copy, `writeEnvelope`, saved views). All are equivalent, including the `hasDir` and timeout values.
- **`writeVia` on `host-fs`** never rejects. It refuses a link or non-file target with exit 73, the same as the sh guard. It uses the same "already exists" text, and it documents its non-atomic gaps honestly.
- **`checkNoLinks` and the export resolvers are now containment-checked through `below()`**, which compares at segment boundaries and case-insensitively on Windows. `hasParentSegment` splits on both separators for Windows paths.
- **The kill flag stays fail-safe.** Only the exact marker `cleared` clears it; an empty file, an unreadable file or any other text is a stop. The GNU behaviour (`rm -f`) is unchanged, and this is tested.
- **A confirmed write keeps its confirm gate.** `remember.ts` refuses to remember a spec that has `write`, so a confirmed write can never be auto-approved.

### Issues

#### Critical
None.

#### Important

**1. The autopilot's duplicate-start guard does not work on Windows.**
- Where: `hooks/data/write-via.ts:107-112` (append is read-then-write) together with `hooks/ap-live.ts:299` (`startedCount(journalNow, stepId) !== 1`).
- What's wrong:
  - `stepId` is deterministic: `sha256(task:attempt)`, from `data/ap-loop.ts:211`. When two sessions pick the same task, both journal a `step.started` with the same id.
  - On Linux, `dd oflag=append` keeps both lines, the count is 2, and both sessions refuse.
  - On `host-fs`, both sessions read X. One writes X+A, the other writes X+B, so one line is lost. Each session then re-reads, counts 1, and hands the step over. The same step is dispatched twice.
- Why it matters: before this PR the autopilot could not start on Windows, because `writeEnvelope` needed `dd`. This PR makes it start (the test at `write-flavor.spec.ts:3098` proves it), so this is a newly reachable safety regression. The `write-via` header documents "can lose a batch" but not this consequence.
- How to fix: either
  - (a) on `host-fs`, have `appendEvents` read the journal back and re-append any of its own lines that are missing (lines
[...]
snapshot check fails, not just the hive start** (`runner.ts`, the retry block). Behaviour is fine, but the commit title "a hive started from the console shows at once" and the CHANGELOG bullet should describe it as a general one-time 1 s re-check.
3. **macOS behaviour changed slightly:** `checkProcs` now answers "not available on this system" instead of spawning `find` and failing (`wf-worktrees.ts:229`). This is a deliberate improvement but a departure from "byte-identical"; say so in the PR body.
4. **Each `host-fs` events flush reads and rewrites the whole Events file** (up to 2 MiB, `activity-io.ts` with `write-via.ts:107`). Acceptable, but worth a sentence in the PR body.
5. **On `host-fs`, export specs still carry a stand-in `argv`** (`['ruflo-console:host-fs', …]`, `event-export.ts:143`, `wf-export.ts:89`), which ends up as the runner's `lastArgv`. Check that no UI surface shows or copies it as a runnable command.

### Deferred-minor triage
- A1, `world.ts:73-74` duplicate normalize: **follow-up** (cosmetic).
- A1, no unit spec for `normalizeFixturePath`: **follow-up** (test-only helper).
- A1, ENOENT shows the normalized path: **follow-up** (test diagnostics only).
- A2 Ruling, mixed separators in `wf-file`/`event-export`: **follow-up** (Windows accepts both; the existing spec pins it).
- A2 Ruling, mission-cost real-script tests failing because of the other plugin's main guard: **follow-up**, with a note in the PR body.
- A2 Ruling, `ap-envelope` refuses backslash roots: acceptable for roots. Its "fails closed" premise does not cover task text, so it is **must-fix before merge** as Important #2 (or gate the autopilot).
- A2, `paths.spec` missing Windows prefix-confusion / mixed-separator / UNC tests: **must-fix before merge**. `below()` now decides containment for `checkNoLinks` and the export resolvers, and adding about four assertions (e.g. `C:\proj` vs `C:\project\x`, UNC, mixed separators) is cheap.
- A2, POSIX odd-input differences (`C:/x` counted as absolute on Linux, etc.): **follow-up**, noted in the PR body (read-only or argv-element effects only).
- A2, `adr.ts:56,75` trim only `/`: **follow-up** (a cwd with a trailing backslash is rare).
- A2, a POSIX-form path with `\..\` on a Windows host: **follow-up**. I checked: `isSafePath` on worktree removal still refuses the drive-letter form, and the other uses are read-only.
- A2, duplicated placement expression; `isRunFile` "/"-only: **follow-up**, listed in the PR body (fails closed).
- A2, flaky events-sweep and model-secrets tests: **follow-up**.
- A2, `pathAllowed` case-sensitive with "/"-only split: **must-fix before merge** together with Important #2, or gate the autopilot.
- A3, home joined with `/` (mixed separators): **follow-up** (only read paths; Windows accepts them).
- A3, no trim in `homeOf`, sequential awaits, spec titles, no wiring test: **follow-up**.
- A4, other `rm` users fail visibly on Windows (Events forget, saved-views forget, tmp cleanup): **follow-up**, listed in the PR body.
- A4, a file already over 4 MiB wedges rotation: **follow-up**. It only occurs if such a file already exists; the fix is to rotate when a write is refused for size.
- A4, `refuse('',0)` used as success, the `touchArgv` import, `isDirReady`, the `put` wrapper: **follow-up**.
- A4, test gaps (the runner's `spec.write` branch, `exportSpecFor` on `host-fs`, journal rotation on `host-fs`): **follow-up**. A runner `spec.write` test is recommended, since that branch is the only route for confirmed exports on Windows.
- A4, `stopNow` relies on the real host accepting an empty-string `fs.write`: **must verify before merge**. It is safety-critical; check it on real Windows during the manual pass the plan requires.
- A4, posix flavor not set explicitly in the new tests: **follow-up**.
- A5, redundant ternary and `platform: unknown`: **follow-up**.
- A6, "expected a queen in…" wording on success: **follow-up** (pre-existing).
- A6, `host.after` never firing would hang the action: **follow-up** (the engine clock; low risk).
- A6, the never-lands test lacks an `ok === false` assertion: **follow-up** (trivial).
- Rulings 1–4 and the A4 kill-flag ruling: sound; no action needed.

### Declined to judge
- CHANGELOG and version bump: the controller adds them at PR time.
- PR-B and PR-C: separate branches.
- Real engine behaviour of `$.fs.write` (whether it makes folders, any size cap) and `$.fs.stat` (whether it reports Windows junctions as `isLink`): the engine's declarations are not in the worktree, so I accepted the code's stated contract. The manual Windows check should confirm it.
- The two-console Events/Timeline lost-batch race: documented by design in `write-via.ts`; there is no safety invariant on those files.
- `clearKill` on `host-fs` without its own `checkNoLinks`: `writeEnvelope` checks the same folder chain just before it, and `viaHostFs` refuses a link at the target.
- Whether sessions/history discovery under `~/.claude/projects` works on Windows: outside A3's stated change (the home lookup).
- The `npx` launcher and other ruflo CLI calls on Windows: outside the plan's Windows scope.
- Cross-OS sharing of a KILL file (WSL and Windows on one folder): fail-safe either way.

### Recommendations
1. Gate the autopilot start on `host-fs` with a clear message. That settles Important #1 and #2 for this PR; do the full fix (read-back verification plus Windows-aware path extraction, deny patterns and `pathAllowed`) as a follow-up PR.
2. Canonicalise Windows workspace keys in `storeKeyOf` and `termStoreKeyOf` (Important #3), and add the Windows containment tests for `below()`.
3. Do the plan's manual Windows checks (Events, ADRs, the Plugins matrix) plus the kill switch with an empty write. Put the before/after test counts in the PR body, along with the known-gaps list (Minor 1, the `rm` users, mission-cost, the macOS process-check note).
4. Reword the A6 commit/CHANGELOG line to describe the general 1 s re-check.

### Assessment
**Ready to merge?** With fixes.
**Reasoning:** The Windows write path is sound and Linux/macOS argv is provably unchanged. But A4 makes the autopilot runnable on Windows, where its duplicate-start guard (#1) and its folder fence and envelope-edit deny (#2) no longer hold, and the plan's Review Focus #2 is unmet (#3). Gating the autopilot on Windows and canonicalising the workspace keys are small, contained changes.

Key files: `C:\Users\mariu\ruflo-wt-console-win\plugins\ruflo-console\hooks\data\write-via.ts`, `...\hooks\ap-live.ts`, `...\hooks\data\ap-guard.ts`, `...\hooks\data\ap-envelope.ts`, `...\hooks\state.ts`, `...\hooks\data\paths.ts`, `...\tests\paths.spec.ts`.
